records.source: וַיְהִ֣י אַֽחֲרֵי כֵ֡ןבָּ֣אוּ בְנֵי־מוֹאָב֩ וּבְנֵ֨י עַמּ֜וֹן וְעִמָּהֶ֧ם׀מֵֽהָעַמּוֹנִ֛ים עַל־יְהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט לַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was after so, came [the] sons of Moab and [the] sons of Ammon and with them some of the Ammonites against Jehoshaphat for battle.
pieces: After this the Moabites and the Ammonites, together with some of the Meunites, came to make war on Jehoshaphat.

L.1: And it happened after this [that] the sons of Moab and the sons of Ammon, and with them some of the Meunites, came against Jehoshaphat for battle.

R.1: Some time later the armies of Moab and Ammon came to fight against Jehoshaphat. Some of the Meunites came with them.

decisions.choice: some of the Meunites
alternatives: some of the Ammonites (the Hebrew text as written)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "some of the Ammonites", which repeats the Ammonites just named. The ancient Greek translation has the Meunites, a people who lived near Mount Seir (26:7; 1 Chronicles 4:41). In Hebrew the two names differ only in the order of two letters, so a copyist could easily confuse them. Verses 10, 22 and 23 name the people of Mount Seir as the third group in the attack, which fits the Meunites.

decisions.choice: after this: after Jehoshaphat's reforms
decisions.reason: "After this" ties the invasion to chapter 19, where Jehoshaphat brought the people back to Yahweh and set judges in the land (19:4-11). The king who has just been faithful now faces a crisis.

decisions.choice: Moab and Ammon: nations east of the Jordan and the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: Moab lay east of the Dead Sea and Ammon to its north-east. Both were counted as descendants of Lot (Genesis 19:37-38), and Israel had been told not to take their land (Deuteronomy 2:9, 19).

decisions.choice: the Moabites and the Ammonites (Balanced); the armies of Moab and Ammon (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "sons of Moab" and "sons of Ammon", the Hebrew way of naming a people. Balanced names the peoples; Readable says "armies", since they came to fight.

records.heading: Jehoshaphat prays for help

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ וַיַּגִּ֤ידוּ לִֽיהוֹשָׁפָט֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בָּ֣א עָלֶ֜יךָ הָמ֥וֹן רָ֛ב מֵעֵ֥בֶר לַיָּ֖ם מֵאֲרָ֑ם וְהִנָּם֙ בְּחַֽצְצ֣וֹן תָּמָ֔ר הִ֖יא עֵ֥ין גֶּֽדִי׃
records.gloss: And came [people] and told Jehoshaphat, saying, is coming against you a multitude great from beyond the sea, from Aram; and behold, they [are] in Hazazon-tamar, that [is] En-gedi.
pieces: Some men came and told Jehoshaphat, "A great army is coming against you from beyond the Dead Sea, from Edom. They are already at Hazazon-tamar, which is En-gedi."

L.2: And [some] came and told Jehoshaphat, saying, "A great multitude is coming against you from beyond the sea, from Edom; and see, they [are] in Hazazon-tamar, that [is] En-gedi."

R.2: Messengers came and told Jehoshaphat, "A huge army is coming to attack you. They are coming from Edom, on the other side of the Dead Sea. They are already at Hazazon-tamar, the town of En-gedi."

decisions.choice: from Edom
alternatives: from Aram (the Hebrew text as written)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "from Aram", the kingdom of the Arameans north-east of Israel. In Hebrew writing the names Aram and Edom differ by one letter, and the two letters (r and d) look very much alike; copyists confused the names elsewhere (2 Kings 16:6). An army that comes "from beyond the sea" to En-gedi comes round the Dead Sea from the east or south, where Edom and Mount Seir lie, and verses 10 and 22 name Mount Seir among the invaders.

decisions.choice: beyond the sea: from the far side of the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: "The sea" here is the Dead Sea, called the Salt Sea in the law (Numbers 34:3). The invaders came from its eastern or southern side.

decisions.choice: Hazazon-tamar, that is En-gedi: an oasis on the west shore of the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: En-gedi was a spring and oasis on the western shore of the Dead Sea, about 25 miles south-east of Jerusalem. Hazazon-tamar ("Hazazon of the palm trees") was its older name (Genesis 14:7). From there a road climbed into the hills of Judah.

decisions.choice: a great multitude: a huge army
decisions.reason: The word means a crowd or throng, often of soldiers (14:10; 1 Kings 20:13). It returns in verses 12, 15 and 24.

decisions.choice: the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the sea (m2) so that readers know which one is meant.

decisions.choice: Hazazon-tamar
decisions.reason: The place is spelled here as in Genesis 14:7, where it is the same town; the Hebrew spelling here differs slightly. Readable adds "the town of" to make clear that En-gedi is the same place.

records.source: וַיִּרָ֕א וַיִּתֵּ֧ן יְהוֹשָׁפָ֛ט אֶת־פָּנָ֖יו לִדְר֣וֹשׁ לַיהוָ֑ה וַיִּקְרָא־צ֖וֹם עַל־כָּל־יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And was afraid and set Jehoshaphat his face to seek Yahweh, and proclaimed a fast over all Judah.
pieces: Jehoshaphat was afraid, and he resolved to seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He proclaimed a fast for all Judah.

L.3: And Jehoshaphat was afraid, and he set his face to seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and he proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah.

R.3: Jehoshaphat was frightened, and he made up his mind to ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help. He told everyone in Judah to fast, to go without food.

decisions.choice: set his face to seek: turned his whole attention to seeking
decisions.reason: To set one's face toward something is to resolve on it. Jehoshaphat's fear did not lead him to panic but to turn to Yahweh.

decisions.choice: to seek Yahweh: to turn to him in prayer for help
decisions.reason: Seeking Yahweh is a key phrase in Chronicles for turning to him in trust and asking his help (7:14; 15:2, 12). Jehoshaphat had done so from the start of his reign (17:4; 19:3).

decisions.choice: a fast: going without food as a sign of humbling and urgent prayer
decisions.reason: Israel fasted in times of danger and grief, to humble themselves before God and to plead with him (Judges 20:26; 1 Samuel 7:6).

decisions.choice: ask the LORD for help; to go without food
decisions.reason: Readable says what "seek" means here (m2) and explains what a fast is (m3).

records.source: וַיִּקָּבְצ֣וּ יְהוּדָ֔ה לְבַקֵּ֖שׁ מֵֽיְהוָ֑ה גַּ֚ם מִכָּל־עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה בָּ֖אוּ לְבַקֵּ֥שׁ אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And gathered Judah to seek from Yahweh; even from all [the] cities of Judah they came to seek Yahweh.
pieces: The people of Judah gathered to seek help from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; they came from every town in Judah to seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.4: And Judah gathered together to seek [help] from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; even from all the cities of Judah they came to seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.4: The people of Judah came together to ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help. They came from every town in Judah to turn to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: to seek from Yahweh ... to seek Yahweh: to ask his help, and to turn to him
decisions.reason: The first phrase has "from": they came to ask something from Yahweh, his help against the invaders. The second has no "from": they came to seek Yahweh himself. The two belong together.

decisions.choice: Judah: the people of Judah
decisions.reason: The name of the land stands for its people, as often.

decisions.choice: help
decisions.reason: Literal brackets and Balanced supplies "help", the object implied by "seek from" (m1).

records.source: וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד יְהוֹשָׁפָ֗ט בִּקְהַ֧ל יְהוּדָ֛ה וִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה לִפְנֵ֖י הֶחָצֵ֥ר הַחֲדָשָֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And stood Jehoshaphat in [the] assembly of Judah and Jerusalem in [the] house of Yahweh, before the court the new.
pieces: Jehoshaphat stood up in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem at the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, in front of the new courtyard.

L.5: And Jehoshaphat stood in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, in front of the new court.

R.5: The people of Judah and Jerusalem were gathered at the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Jehoshaphat stood up in front of them, in front of the new courtyard.

decisions.choice: the new court: a courtyard of the temple, rebuilt or newly made
decisions.reason: The text does not say which court this was. It may be the great outer court of the temple (4:9), renewed in Jehoshaphat's or Asa's time. The king stood where the gathered people could see and hear him.

decisions.choice: Jehoshaphat stood in the assembly: as Solomon did when he prayed at the temple's dedication
decisions.reason: Solomon stood before the assembly of Israel in the court of the temple and prayed (6:12-13). Jehoshaphat's prayer, which follows, calls on the promise Solomon prayed for (verse 9).

decisions.choice: two sentences; the temple
decisions.reason: Readable first says the people were gathered, then that the king stood before them. It says "temple" for "house of the LORD", as these books do.

records.source: וַיֹּאמַ֗ר יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י אֲבֹתֵ֨ינוּ֙ הֲלֹ֨א אַתָּֽה־ה֤וּא אֱלֹהִים֙ בַּשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְאַתָּ֣ה מוֹשֵׁ֔ל בְּכֹ֖ל מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וּבְיָדְךָ֙ כֹּ֣חַ וּגְבוּרָ֔ה וְאֵ֥ין עִמְּךָ֖ לְהִתְיַצֵּֽב׃
records.gloss: And he said, Yahweh, God of our fathers, [are] not you he, God in the heavens? And you [are] ruling over all [the] kingdoms of the nations, and in your hand [are] power and might, and there is not with you to stand.
pieces: He said, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of our ancestors, are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not God in heaven? You rule over every kingdom of the nations. In {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand are power and might, and no one is able to withstand {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.6: And he said, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of our fathers, are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not God in heaven? And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rule over all the kingdoms of the nations, and in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand [are] power and might, and [there is] no one to stand against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.6: He prayed, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of our ancestors, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are God in heaven. You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations. You are strong and mighty, and no one can stand against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: are you not God in heaven?: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: The question is a confession of faith: Yahweh is the God who rules from heaven. The prayer opens by stating who God is before it states the need.

decisions.choice: in your hand are power and might: the words of David's prayer
decisions.reason: David praised Yahweh with the same words when the people gave for the temple (1 Chronicles 29:11-12). Jehoshaphat calls on the same God who rules over all.

decisions.choice: you rule over all the kingdoms of the nations: the invading nations are under God's rule
decisions.reason: Moab, Ammon and Seir are among the kingdoms Yahweh rules. No army can stand against him, so the danger is not beyond his power.

decisions.choice: there is no one to stand against you: no one can resist you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "there is not with you to take a stand". "With" here means "against" (as in 14:10), and the verb is used of standing one's ground in battle.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
decisions.reason: Readable states what the question means (m1). It says "strong and mighty" for "power and might in your hand".

records.source: הֲלֹ֣א׀אַתָּ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ הוֹרַ֨שְׁתָּ֙ אֶת־יֹשְׁבֵי֙ הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את מִלִּפְנֵ֖י עַמְּךָ֣ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽתִּתְּנָ֗הּ לְזֶ֛רַע אַבְרָהָ֥ם אֹֽהַבְךָ֖ לְעוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: [Did] not you, our God, dispossess [the] inhabitants of the land the this from before your people Israel, and you gave it to [the] offspring of Abraham your friend forever?
pieces: Our God, was it not {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who drove out the people living in this land as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel came in, and gave it for all time to the descendants of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} friend Abraham?

L.7: Did {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not, our God, drive out the inhabitants of this land before {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel, and give it to the offspring of Abraham {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} friend forever?

R.7: You are our God. You drove out the people who lived in this land so that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel could have it. You gave it forever to the descendants of Abraham, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} friend.

decisions.choice: did you not ...?: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, the question recalls what everyone knows to be true: God gave Israel this land.

decisions.choice: Abraham your friend: as in Isaiah 41:8
decisions.reason: God calls Israel "the offspring of Abraham, my friend" in Isaiah 41:8. The Hebrew word means "the one who loves you"; it speaks of the close bond God made with Abraham. The land was promised to him and his offspring (Genesis 12:7; 13:15).

decisions.choice: drive out: dispossess
decisions.reason: The verb means to take possession by driving out the people who held the land (Deuteronomy 9:3-5).

decisions.choice: forever: the gift was for all time
decisions.reason: "Forever" goes with the gift of the land: it was given to Abraham's offspring for all time (Genesis 13:15). The invaders now threaten that gift (verse 11).

decisions.choice: statements instead of a question
decisions.reason: Readable states what the question means (m1), as in verse 6.

records.source: וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ־בָ֑הּ וַיִּבְנ֨וּ לְךָ֧׀בָּ֛הּ מִקְדָּ֖שׁ לְשִׁמְךָ֥ לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And they dwelt in it, and they built for you in it a sanctuary for your name, saying,
pieces: They have lived in it and built {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} a sanctuary in it for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, saying,

L.8: And they lived in it, and they built {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} a sanctuary in it for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, saying,

R.8: They have lived in this land. They built a temple in it to honor {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, and they said,

decisions.choice: a sanctuary: the temple, the holy place
decisions.reason: The word means a holy place. Here it is the temple built by Solomon (1 Chronicles 22:19; 28:10).

decisions.choice: for your name: the place where God is known and called on
decisions.reason: Yahweh chose the temple as the place for his name, where his people could call on him (6:20; 7:16).

decisions.choice: saying: the prayer of verse 9 is what they said when they built it
decisions.reason: "Saying" introduces words the builders spoke, which sum up Solomon's prayer at the dedication (6:28-30, 34-35). The sentence runs on into verse 9.

decisions.choice: a temple to honor your name
decisions.reason: Readable says "temple" for "sanctuary" and explains "for your name" (m2).

records.source: אִם־תָּב֨וֹא עָלֵ֜ינוּ רָעָ֗ה חֶרֶב֮ שְׁפוֹט֮ וְדֶ֣בֶר וְרָעָב֒ נַֽעַמְדָ֞ה לִפְנֵ֨יהַבַּ֤יִת הַזֶּה֙ וּלְפָנֶ֔יךָ כִּ֥י שִׁמְךָ֖ בַּבַּ֣יִת הַזֶּ֑ה וְנִזְעַ֥ק אֵלֶ֛יךָ מִצָּרָתֵ֖נוּ וְתִשְׁמַ֥ע וְתוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃
records.gloss: If comes upon us calamity, sword, judgment, or pestilence or famine, we will stand before the house the this and before you, for your name [is] in the house the this, and we will cry out to you from our distress, and you will hear and save.
pieces: 'If disaster comes upon us, whether the sword of judgment, or disease, or famine, we will stand before this house and in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} presence, since this house bears {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name. We will cry out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in our trouble, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will hear and save us.'

L.9: 'If calamity comes upon us, sword, judgment, or pestilence, or famine, we will stand before this house and before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name [is] in this house, and we will cry out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} from our distress, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will hear and save.'

R.9: 'Trouble may come on us. War may come as a punishment, or disease, or hunger. Then we will stand in front of this temple and before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name is here in this temple. We will cry out to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in our trouble, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will hear us and rescue us.'

decisions.choice: if disaster comes upon us ...: Solomon's prayer in brief
decisions.reason: The words sum up Solomon's prayer at the dedication of the temple: sword, plague and famine (6:24-30), and the promise that God would hear prayer made toward the house where his name is (6:20; 7:13-15).

decisions.choice: sword, judgment: the sword as God's judgment, or two separate troubles
alternatives: sword, judgment, pestilence or famine (four troubles)
decisions.reason: The two words stand side by side with no "and" between them. They may mean "the sword of judgment", war sent as a punishment, or "sword" and "judgment" as two of the troubles in the list. The meaning is much the same either way.

decisions.choice: pestilence: deadly disease, plague
decisions.reason: The word names a deadly epidemic, one of the judgments of the covenant (Leviticus 26:25; 2 Chronicles 7:13).

decisions.choice: you will hear and save: the expected answer
decisions.reason: The verbs are the people's confident expectation, based on God's promise (7:14-15).

decisions.choice: single quotation marks
decisions.reason: These are words the builders said (verse 8), quoted inside Jehoshaphat's prayer, so they take single quotation marks.

decisions.choice: several short sentences
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long "if ... then" sentence into shorter sentences.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֡ה הִנֵּה֩ בְנֵֽי־עַמּ֨וֹן וּמוֹאָ֜ב וְהַר־שֵׂעִ֗יר אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא־נָתַ֤תָּה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לָב֣וֹא בָהֶ֔ם בְּבֹאָ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם כִּ֛י סָ֥רוּ מֵעֲלֵיהֶ֖ם וְלֹ֥א הִשְׁמִידֽוּם׃
records.gloss: And now, behold, [the] sons of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir, whom not you let Israel to go into them when they came from [the] land of Egypt, for they turned aside from them and not destroyed them,
pieces: But now look at the people of Ammon, Moab and Mount Seir. You would not let Israel invade them when Israel came out of the land of Egypt, so Israel turned away from them and did not destroy them,

L.10: And now, see, the sons of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir, whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did not let Israel invade when they came from the land of Egypt, for they turned aside from them and did not destroy them,

R.10: Now look at the armies of Ammon, Moab and Mount Seir. When our people came out of Egypt, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did not let them attack these nations. So Israel went around them and did not destroy them.

decisions.choice: you did not let Israel invade them: as told in Numbers and Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: On the way from Egypt, Yahweh told Israel not to attack Edom, Moab or Ammon, because he had given them their lands (Deuteronomy 2:4-9, 19). When Edom refused Israel passage, Israel turned away (Numbers 20:14-21).

decisions.choice: Mount Seir: the hill country of Edom
decisions.reason: Seir was the mountain land of Edom, south-east of the Dead Sea, where Esau's descendants lived (Genesis 36:8-9). Its people are the third group of invaders (see the note on verse 2).

decisions.choice: they turned aside from them: Israel turned away from these nations
decisions.reason: "They" is Israel, which went around these peoples instead of destroying them. The prayer sets Israel's restraint then against the invaders' attack now (verse 11).

decisions.choice: Israel
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Israel as the subject of "turned away" (m3). Readable ends with a full stop and starts verse 11 as a new sentence; Literal and Balanced end with a comma, since the sentence runs on.

records.source: וְהִ֨נֵּה־הֵ֔ם גֹּמְלִ֖ים עָלֵ֑ינוּ לָבוֹא֙ לְגָ֣רְשֵׁ֔נוּ מִיְּרֻשָּׁתְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֽוֹרַשְׁתָּֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: and behold, they [are] repaying us by coming to drive us out from your possession which you gave us to possess.
pieces: and see how they repay us: they are coming to drive us out of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} possession, the land {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave us to hold as our own.

L.11: and see, they are repaying us by coming to drive us out of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} possession, which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave us to possess.

R.11: And now see how they pay us back! They are coming to force us out of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} land, the land {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave us to keep.

decisions.choice: repaying us: paying back good with evil
decisions.reason: The verb means to deal with someone or to repay. Israel spared these nations (verse 10), and now they repay that kindness with an invasion.

decisions.choice: your possession: the land belongs to God
decisions.reason: The land is called God's possession, which he gave to Israel to hold (Leviticus 25:23). An attack on it is an attack on what is his.

decisions.choice: which you gave us to possess: the verb of verse 7
decisions.reason: The verb is the same one used in verse 7 for driving out the land's earlier inhabitants. The invaders want to do to Judah what God did for Israel, but God gave the land to Israel.

decisions.choice: the land
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name what the "possession" is.

records.source: אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ הֲלֹ֣א תִשְׁפָּט־בָּ֔ם כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין בָּ֨נוּ֙ כֹּ֔חַ לִ֠פְנֵי הֶהָמ֥וֹן הָרָ֛ב הַזֶּ֖ה הַבָּ֣א עָלֵ֑ינוּ וַאֲנַ֗חְנוּ לֹ֤א נֵדַע֙ מַֽה־נַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה כִּ֥י עָלֶ֖יךָ עֵינֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: Our God, [will] not you judge them? For there is not in us strength before the multitude the great the this the [one] coming against us, and we, not we know what we will do, for on you [are] our eyes.
pieces: Our God, will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not judge them? We have no strength to face this great army that is coming against us. We have no idea what we should do, but our eyes are turned toward {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

L.12: Our God, will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not judge them? For [there is] no strength in us before this great multitude that is coming against us, and we, we do not know what we should do, for our eyes [are] on {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

R.12: Our God, punish them! We are not strong enough to fight this huge army that is attacking us. We do not know what we should do. So we are looking to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for help."

decisions.choice: judge them: act as judge against them, punish them
decisions.reason: To judge here is to give a verdict and carry it out: to deal with the invaders as their wrong deserves (1 Samuel 24:13).

decisions.choice: will you not judge them?: a plea that expects God to act
decisions.reason: The question is a request: the king asks God to do what he as judge of all the nations rightly does (verse 6).

decisions.choice: our eyes are on you: we look to you and wait for your help
decisions.reason: To have one's eyes on someone is to look to him in hope and dependence, as a servant watches his master's hand (Psalm 123:2; 25:15).

decisions.choice: we do not know what to do: we are helpless
decisions.reason: The emphatic "we" sets the people's helplessness against God's power: they have no plan, only their trust in him.

decisions.choice: punish them!; we are looking to you for help
decisions.reason: Readable gives the plea as a request (m2) and explains the picture of the eyes (m3).

records.source: וְכָ֨ל־יְהוּדָ֔ה עֹמְדִ֖ים לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה גַּם־טַפָּ֖ם נְשֵׁיהֶ֥ם וּבְנֵיהֶֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And all Judah [were] standing before Yahweh, also their little ones, their wives, and their sons.
pieces: All Judah stood before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, together with their little ones, their wives and their children.

L.13: And all Judah [was] standing before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, also their little ones, their wives, and their sons.

R.13: All the men of Judah stood there before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, with their wives and children, even the little ones.

decisions.choice: all Judah with their little ones, wives and children: the whole community before God
decisions.reason: Everyone was in danger, so everyone came to stand before Yahweh: men, women and children together. The whole people waits for God's answer (compare Joel 2:16).

decisions.choice: little ones ... sons: small children and older children
decisions.reason: "Little ones" are children too young to walk far; "sons" here is the common word for children in general, boys and girls.

decisions.choice: children
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "children" for "sons" (m2). Readable says "the men of Judah" because the wives and children are named beside them.

records.source: וְיַחֲזִיאֵ֡ל בֶּן־זְכַרְיָ֡הוּ בֶּן־בְּ֠נָיָה בֶּן־יְעִיאֵ֧ל בֶּן־מַתַּנְיָ֛ה הַלֵּוִ֖י מִן־בְּנֵ֣י אָסָ֑ף הָיְתָ֤ה עָלָיו֙ ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֔ה בְּת֖וֹךְ הַקָּהָֽל׃
records.gloss: And Jahaziel son of Zechariah son of Benaiah son of Jeiel son of Mattaniah, the Levite, from [the] sons of Asaph, came upon him [the] Spirit of Yahweh in [the] midst of the assembly.
pieces: Then the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came upon Jahaziel son of Zechariah, son of Benaiah, son of Jeiel, son of Mattaniah, a Levite of the family of Asaph, there in the middle of the assembly.

L.14: And Jahaziel son of Zechariah, son of Benaiah, son of Jeiel, son of Mattaniah, the Levite, of the sons of Asaph: the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came upon him in the midst of the assembly.

R.14: Then the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on a man in the crowd named Jahaziel. He was a Levite from the family of Asaph. His father was Zechariah, and his earlier ancestors were Benaiah, Jeiel and Mattaniah.

decisions.choice: Jahaziel ... came upon him: the man is named first
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts the man and his family line first and then says what happened to him. The long line of ancestors shows that the speaker was a known Levite, not a stranger.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of Yahweh came upon him: God gave him a message to speak
decisions.reason: In Chronicles the Spirit comes upon a person so that he speaks for God (15:1; 24:20; 1 Chronicles 12:19). Jahaziel was not a known prophet, but God spoke through him.

decisions.choice: the sons of Asaph: a family of temple singers
decisions.reason: Asaph was one of the leaders of the singers David appointed (1 Chronicles 16:5; 25:1-2). Their music is called prophesying (1 Chronicles 25:1-2), and here one of them brings God's word.

decisions.choice: the Spirit first; the ancestors after
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable start with what happened, as English usually does, and give the family line after the name. Readable lists the ancestors in a separate sentence.

records.heading: God answers and gives victory

records.source: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הַקְשִׁ֤יבוּ כָל־יְהוּדָה֙ וְיֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְהַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֑ט כֹּֽה־אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה לָכֶ֗ם אַ֠תֶּם אַל־תִּֽירְא֤וּ וְאַל־תֵּחַ֨תּוּ֙ מִפְּנֵ֨י הֶהָמ֤וֹן הָרָב֙ הַזֶּ֔ה כִּ֣י לֹ֥א לָכֶ֛ם הַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה כִּ֥י לֵאלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And he said, Listen, all Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem and the king Jehoshaphat: thus says Yahweh to you, you, do not fear and do not be dismayed because of the multitude the great the this, for not to you [is] the battle but to God.
pieces: He said, "Listen, all Judah, people of Jerusalem, and King Jehoshaphat! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this to you: 'Do not be afraid or lose heart because of this great army, for the battle is not yours; it belongs to God.

L.15: And he said, "Listen, all Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, and King Jehoshaphat: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to you: 'You, do not fear and do not be dismayed because of this great multitude, for the battle [is] not yours, but God's.

R.15: He said, "Listen, everyone in Judah and Jerusalem, and you too, King Jehoshaphat! This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says to you: 'Do not be afraid. Do not lose courage because of this huge army. This is not your battle. It is God's battle.

decisions.choice: do not fear and do not be dismayed: God's encouragement to his leaders
decisions.reason: These are the words Yahweh spoke to Joshua before battle (Deuteronomy 31:8; Joshua 8:1; 10:25) and David spoke to Solomon (1 Chronicles 22:13; 28:20).

decisions.choice: the battle is not yours but God's: God himself fights
decisions.reason: David told Goliath that "the battle belongs to Yahweh" (1 Samuel 17:47). Judah will not need to fight at all (verse 17); God will win the battle.

decisions.choice: be dismayed: be shattered, lose courage
decisions.reason: The verb means to be broken or crushed, and is used of courage that collapses in terror.

decisions.choice: thus says Yahweh: the prophet's formula
decisions.reason: The words mark what follows as Yahweh's own message, which runs through verse 17.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD / The LORD says this / This is what the LORD says
decisions.reason: The messenger formula has one wording at each level throughout these books. Yahweh's words take single quotation marks inside Jahaziel's speech.

decisions.choice: lose heart (Balanced); lose courage (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Joshua 8:1. Balanced and Readable leave out the emphatic "you", which Literal keeps.

records.source: מָחָר֙ רְד֣וּ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם הִנָּ֥ם עֹלִ֖ים בְּמַעֲלֵ֣ה הַצִּ֑יץ וּמְצָאתֶ֤ם אֹתָם֙ בְּס֣וֹף הַנַּ֔חַל פְּנֵ֖י מִדְבַּ֥ר יְרוּאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Tomorrow go down against them; behold, they [are] coming up by [the] ascent of Ziz, and you will find them at [the] end of the valley, before [the] wilderness of Jeruel.
pieces: Tomorrow go down against them. They will be coming up by the Ascent of Ziz; you will find them where the valley ends, opposite the wilderness of Jeruel.

L.16: Tomorrow go down against them. See, they [are] coming up by the ascent of Ziz, and you will find them at the end of the valley, facing the wilderness of Jeruel.

R.16: Tomorrow go down to meet them. They will be climbing up the pass of Ziz. You will find them where the valley ends, near the desert of Jeruel.

decisions.choice: the ascent of Ziz: a pass climbing from the Dead Sea into the hills of Judah
decisions.reason: The road from En-gedi climbs steeply from the Dead Sea shore into the hill country toward Tekoa (verse 20). The exact place of Ziz is not known.

decisions.choice: the valley: a stream bed, dry for much of the year
decisions.reason: The word names a valley cut by a stream that flows only in the rainy season, common in the wilderness of Judah.

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Jeruel: dry land near Tekoa
decisions.reason: The place is named only here. It lay in the wilderness between En-gedi and Tekoa.

decisions.choice: they are coming up: a description of what they will be doing tomorrow
decisions.reason: The participle describes the enemy's movement at the time Judah goes down, not at the moment of speaking.

decisions.choice: pass; desert
decisions.reason: Readable says "pass" for "ascent" and "desert" for "wilderness".

records.source: לֹ֥א לָכֶ֖ם לְהִלָּחֵ֣ם בָּזֹ֑את הִתְיַצְּב֣וּ עִמְד֡וּ וּרְא֣וּ אֶת־יְשׁוּעַת֩ יְהוָ֨ה עִמָּכֶ֜ם יְהוּדָ֣ה וִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אַל־תִּֽירְאוּ֙ וְאַל־תֵּחַ֔תּוּ מָחָר֙ צְא֣וּ לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיהוָ֖ה עִמָּכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Not for you to fight in this; station yourselves, stand, and see [the] salvation of Yahweh with you, Judah and Jerusalem. Do not fear and do not be dismayed; tomorrow go out before them, and Yahweh [will be] with you.
pieces: You will not need to fight in this battle. Hold your ground, stand firm, and watch how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will save you, Judah and Jerusalem. Do not be afraid or lose heart. Tomorrow go out to face them, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be with you.'"

L.17: [It is] not for you to fight in this [battle]. Station yourselves, stand, and see the salvation of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with you, Judah and Jerusalem. Do not fear and do not be dismayed. Tomorrow go out before them, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [will be] with you.'"

R.17: You will not have to fight this battle. Stay where you are, stand still, and you will see {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rescue you, people of Judah and Jerusalem. Do not be afraid. Do not lose courage. Tomorrow go out to face them, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be with you.'"

decisions.choice: station yourselves and see the salvation of Yahweh: Moses' words at the sea
decisions.reason: Moses told Israel at the Red Sea, "Station yourselves and see the salvation of Yahweh" (Exodus 14:13), and Yahweh fought for them while they stood still (Exodus 14:14). Jahaziel's message repeats those words, adding "stand" and "with you": Judah too will watch God win the battle. The wording here follows Exodus 14:13.

decisions.choice: station yourselves, stand: take your position and stand firm
decisions.reason: The first verb is used of soldiers taking their places for battle. Here they take their places only to watch, not to fight.

decisions.choice: the salvation of Yahweh: Yahweh's rescue, his victory
decisions.reason: The word means rescue from danger, and in battle the victory God gives (Exodus 14:13; 1 Samuel 14:45).

decisions.choice: Yahweh will be with you: a promise
decisions.reason: There is no verb in Hebrew; the setting makes it a promise for tomorrow's march. Yahweh speaks of himself by name, as often.

decisions.choice: Hold your ground ... watch how the LORD will save you (Balanced); Stay where you are ... you will see the LORD rescue you (Readable)
decisions.reason: The words follow the wording of Exodus 14:13 at each level (m1).

decisions.choice: [battle]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "battle", which the Hebrew "in this" implies.

records.source: וַיִּקֹּ֧ד יְהוֹשָׁפָ֛ט אַפַּ֖יִם אָ֑רְצָה וְכָל־יְהוּדָ֞ה וְיֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם נָֽפְלוּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה לְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֖ת לַיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And bowed Jehoshaphat face to [the] ground, and all Judah and [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem fell before Yahweh to worship Yahweh.
pieces: Jehoshaphat bowed down with his face to the ground, and all Judah and the people of Jerusalem fell down before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.18: And Jehoshaphat bowed [his] face to the ground, and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell down before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.18: Jehoshaphat bowed down with his face to the ground. All the people of Judah and Jerusalem also bowed down before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and worshiped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: bowed his face to the ground: worship and humble thanks
decisions.reason: To bow low with the face to the ground was the deepest sign of honor and submission. The king and people answer God's promise with worship before the victory is seen.

decisions.choice: to worship: to bow down in worship
decisions.reason: The verb means to bow down low; with "before Yahweh" it is the act of worship (7:3).

decisions.choice: worshiped him
decisions.reason: Readable says "him" for the second mention of the divine name, to avoid repeating it in a short sentence.

records.source: וַיָּקֻ֧מוּ הַלְוִיִּ֛ם מִן־בְּנֵ֥י הַקְּהָתִ֖ים וּמִן־בְּנֵ֣י הַקָּרְחִ֑ים לְהַלֵּ֗ל לַיהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּק֥וֹל גָּד֖וֹל לְמָֽעְלָה׃
records.gloss: And stood up the Levites from [the] sons of the Kohathites and from [the] sons of the Korahites to praise Yahweh God of Israel with a voice great upward.
pieces: Then the Levites from the Kohathites and the Korahites stood up to praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, with a very loud voice.

L.19: And the Levites, of the sons of the Kohathites and of the sons of the Korahites, stood up to praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, with a great voice, on high.

R.19: Then some of the Levites from the families of Kohath and Korah stood up. They praised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, with very loud voices.

decisions.choice: the Kohathites and the Korahites: Levite families of singers
decisions.reason: Kohath was a son of Levi, and Korah was one of his descendants (Exodus 6:16-21). Sons of Korah served among the temple singers, and several psalms bear their name (Psalm 42:1).

decisions.choice: with a great voice upward: very loudly
decisions.reason: "Upward" adds force to "a great voice": they praised as loudly as they could, their voices rising high.

decisions.choice: praise before the battle: thanks for what God has promised
decisions.reason: The Levites praise God before anything has happened, because they trust the promise of verses 15-17.

decisions.choice: a very loud voice
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "on high"; Balanced and Readable express the idea as "very loud" (m2).

records.source: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וַיֵּצְא֖וּ לְמִדְבַּ֣ר תְּק֑וֹעַ וּבְצֵאתָ֞ם עָמַ֣ד יְהוֹשָׁפָ֗ט וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ שְׁמָע֗וּנִי יְהוּדָה֙ וְיֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם הַאֲמִ֜ינוּ בַּיהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם֙ וְתֵ֣אָמֵ֔נוּ הַאֲמִ֥ינוּ בִנְבִיאָ֖יו וְהַצְלִֽיחוּ׃
records.gloss: And they rose early in the morning and went out to [the] wilderness of Tekoa; and as they went out, stood Jehoshaphat and said, Hear me, Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem: believe in Yahweh your God and you will be established; believe in his prophets and succeed.
pieces: Early in the morning they set out for the wilderness of Tekoa. As they were leaving, Jehoshaphat stood up and said, "Hear me, Judah and people of Jerusalem! Hold firm in your trust in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and you will be held firm. Trust {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} prophets, and you will succeed."

L.20: And they rose early in the morning and went out to the wilderness of Tekoa; and as they went out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, "Hear me, Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem! Believe in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and you will be established; believe {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} prophets, and succeed."

R.20: Early the next morning they went out to the desert near Tekoa. As they were leaving, Jehoshaphat stood up and said, "Listen to me, people of Judah and Jerusalem! Trust firmly in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and you will stand firm. Believe what {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} prophets say, and you will succeed."

decisions.choice: believe ... and you will be established: Isaiah's word to Ahaz
decisions.reason: Isaiah told King Ahaz, "If you do not believe, you will not be established" (Isaiah 7:9). Both verbs come from one root meaning to be firm: to trust is to hold firm, and those who trust will be held firm. Jehoshaphat puts the same word as a promise.

decisions.choice: believe his prophets: trust the message God has sent through them
decisions.reason: The prophets here include Jahaziel, whose message the king tells the people to trust (verses 15-17).

decisions.choice: and succeed: a promise
decisions.reason: The command "succeed" after "believe" states the result: if they trust, they will succeed.

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Tekoa: dry land south of Bethlehem
decisions.reason: Tekoa was a town in the hills about ten miles south of Jerusalem, at the edge of the wilderness that falls toward the Dead Sea; the prophet Amos came from there (Amos 1:1).

decisions.choice: Hold firm in your trust ... you will be held firm (Balanced); Trust firmly ... you will stand firm (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wordplay is rendered as in Isaiah 7:9 at each level (m1).

records.source: וַיִּוָּעַץ֙ אֶל־הָעָ֔ם וַיַּעֲמֵ֤ד מְשֹֽׁרֲרִים֙ לַיהוָ֔ה וּֽמְהַֽלְלִ֖ים לְהַדְרַת־קֹ֑דֶשׁ בְּצֵאת֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הֶֽחָל֔וּץ וְאֹֽמְרִים֙ הוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י לְעוֹלָ֖ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he consulted with the people and appointed singers to Yahweh and [ones] praising in [the] splendor of holiness, as [they] went out before the armed [men], and saying, Give thanks to Yahweh, for to forever [is] his steadfast love.
pieces: After consulting with the people, he appointed singers to sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and to praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in holy splendor as they went out ahead of the army, saying, "Give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} thanks, for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love lasts forever."

L.21: And he took counsel with the people, and he appointed singers to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and [ones] praising in [the] splendor of holiness, as they went out before the armed men, and saying, "Give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love [is] forever."

R.21: Jehoshaphat talked with the people about what to do. Then he appointed singers to sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Dressed in holy robes, they marched out ahead of the army, singing, "Thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! His faithful love lasts forever."

decisions.choice: in the splendor of holiness: in holy attire
alternatives: praising the splendor of his holiness
decisions.reason: The phrase can describe the singers, dressed in the holy garments of worship, or the splendor of God's holiness in which he is praised (Psalm 29:2; 1 Chronicles 16:29). Since the singers are the subject, this translation takes it of their dress.

decisions.choice: give thanks to Yahweh, for his loyal love is forever: the refrain of temple praise
decisions.reason: These are the opening words of Psalm 136 (also 106:1; 118:1), sung when the ark came to Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 16:34) and at the temple's dedication (5:13; 7:3). The refrain is worded here as in 5:13 and 7:3.

decisions.choice: loyal love: chesed
decisions.reason: The word is the faithful, loyal love that keeps a covenant (7:3).

decisions.choice: before the armed men: the singers led the march
decisions.reason: The singers went out ahead of the soldiers, as the ark and the priests led Israel at Jericho (Joshua 6:8-9). The battle was God's, and praise led the way.

decisions.choice: he consulted with the people: he took counsel with them
decisions.reason: The verb means to take advice together. The king planned the march with the people's leaders.

decisions.choice: loyal love [is] forever (Literal); loyal love lasts forever (Balanced); faithful love lasts forever (Readable)
decisions.reason: The refrain is worded as in 1 Chronicles 16:34 and the Psalms it quotes, as at 5:13 and 7:3: "loyal love" at Literal and Balanced, "faithful love" at Readable.

decisions.choice: dressed in holy robes
decisions.reason: Readable says what the singers wore, following m1, and splits the sentence.

records.source: וּבְעֵת֩ הֵחֵ֨לּוּ בְרִנָּ֜ה וּתְהִלָּ֗ה נָתַ֣ן יְהוָ֣ה׀מְ֠אָֽרְבִים עַל־בְּנֵ֨י עַמּ֜וֹן מוֹאָ֧ב וְהַר־שֵׂעִ֛יר הַבָּאִ֥ים לִֽיהוּדָ֖ה וַיִּנָּגֵֽפוּ׃
records.gloss: And at [the] time [when] they began with ringing cry and praise, set Yahweh ambushers against [the] sons of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir, the [ones] coming against Judah; and they were struck down.
pieces: The moment they began their shouts of joy and praise, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} set ambushes against the invaders from Ammon, Moab and Mount Seir who had come to attack Judah, and they were routed.

L.22: And at the time they began with a ringing cry and praise, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} set ambushers against the sons of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir who were coming against Judah, and they were struck down.

R.22: As soon as they began to sing and praise, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent surprise attacks against the armies of Ammon, Moab and Mount Seir who had come to attack Judah. So the invaders were defeated.

decisions.choice: ambushers: men lying in wait, whose identity is not said
decisions.reason: The text says only that Yahweh set men in ambush. They may have been groups within the invading armies, who began the fighting among themselves that verse 23 describes, or a force sent by God. The point is that God, not Judah, struck the enemy.

decisions.choice: at the time they began: at the very moment
decisions.reason: The timing matters: the attack came as soon as the singing started. Praise came first, and God acted.

decisions.choice: a ringing cry: a joyful shout or song
decisions.reason: The word names a loud cry, here a shout of joy and praise.

decisions.choice: they were struck down: the invaders were defeated
decisions.reason: The verb means to be struck or routed in battle (1 Samuel 4:2). Its subject is the invaders.

decisions.choice: surprise attacks
decisions.reason: Readable says "surprise attacks", which keeps the sense of an ambush without saying who carried them out (m1).

records.source: וַ֠יַּֽעַמְדוּ בְּנֵ֨י עַמּ֧וֹן וּמוֹאָ֛ב עַל־יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הַר־שֵׂעִ֖יר לְהַחֲרִ֣ים וּלְהַשְׁמִ֑יד וּכְכַלּוֹתָם֙ בְּיוֹשְׁבֵ֣י שֵׂעִ֔יר עָזְר֥וּ אִישׁ־בְּרֵעֵ֖הוּ לְמַשְׁחִֽית׃
records.gloss: And rose up [the] sons of Ammon and Moab against [the] inhabitants of Mount Seir to devote to destruction and to destroy; and when they finished with [the] inhabitants of Seir, they helped each against his neighbor to destruction.
pieces: The men of Ammon and Moab turned against the people of Mount Seir to devote them to destruction and wipe them out. When they had finished off the people of Seir, they all helped to destroy one another.

L.23: And the sons of Ammon and Moab rose up against the inhabitants of Mount Seir to devote [them] to destruction and to wipe [them] out; and when they had finished with the inhabitants of Seir, they helped, each against his neighbor, to destroy.

R.23: The armies of Ammon and Moab turned against the people of Mount Seir and destroyed them completely. When they had finished killing the people of Seir, they began to kill each other.

decisions.choice: devote to destruction: destroy completely
decisions.reason: The verb is the word for devoting something to God by destroying it completely (Deuteronomy 7:2). Here the invaders do it to one another: the word stresses how complete the slaughter was.

decisions.choice: they helped, each against his neighbor, to destroy: they turned on one another
decisions.reason: The expression is unusual: each man "helped" to destroy his fellow. The allies who came together against Judah ended by destroying each other.

decisions.choice: enemies destroying one another: as in Gideon's and Saul's battles
decisions.reason: God threw Israel's enemies into confusion so that they struck one another (Judges 7:22; 1 Samuel 14:20).

decisions.choice: destroyed them completely
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the two verbs together (m1).

records.source: וִֽיהוּדָ֛ה בָּ֥א עַל־הַמִּצְפֶּ֖ה לַמִּדְבָּ֑ר וַיִּפְנוּ֙ אֶל־הֶ֣הָמ֔וֹן וְהִנָּ֧ם פְּגָרִ֛ים נֹפְלִ֥ים אַ֖רְצָה וְאֵ֥ין פְּלֵיטָֽה׃
records.gloss: And Judah came to the watchtower of the wilderness, and they turned to the multitude, and behold, they [were] corpses fallen to [the] ground, and there was not an escaped [one].
pieces: When Judah came to the lookout point over the wilderness and looked toward the great army, there were only dead bodies lying on the ground; no one had escaped.

L.24: And Judah came to the watchtower of the wilderness, and they turned toward the multitude, and see, they [were] corpses fallen to the ground, and [there was] no one escaping.

R.24: The men of Judah came to the place where they could look out over the desert. They looked toward the huge army, and saw only dead bodies lying on the ground. Not one enemy soldier had escaped.

decisions.choice: the watchtower of the wilderness: a lookout point
decisions.reason: The word means a place for watching, a height or tower from which one could see across the wilderness toward the Dead Sea.

decisions.choice: and see, they were corpses: the sudden sight
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "see" (hinneh) puts the reader beside the men of Judah as they look: where they expected an army, they saw only bodies.

decisions.choice: no one escaping: no survivor
decisions.reason: The word names a remnant that escapes a disaster. None of the invaders got away.

decisions.choice: only
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "only" to bring out the surprise of the scene (m2). Readable says "enemy soldier" for clarity.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֨א יְהוֹשָׁפָ֣ט וְעַמּוֹ֮ לָבֹ֣ז אֶת־שְׁלָלָם֒ וַיִּמְצְאוּ֩ בָהֶ֨ם לָרֹ֜ב וּרְכ֤וּשׁ וּפְגָרִים֙ וּכְלֵ֣י חֲמֻד֔וֹת וַיְנַצְּל֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם לְאֵ֣ין מַשָּׂ֑א וַיִּֽהְי֞וּ יָמִ֧ים שְׁלוֹשָׁ֛ה בֹּזְזִ֥ים אֶת־הַשָּׁלָ֖ל כִּ֥י רַב־הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And came Jehoshaphat and his people to plunder their spoil, and they found among them in abundance goods and corpses and articles of preciousness, and they stripped for themselves until there was not carrying; and they were days three plundering the spoil, for much [was] it.
pieces: When Jehoshaphat and his troops came to take the spoil, they found among them, with the dead, great quantities of goods and valuable things. They took more for themselves than they could carry. There was so much spoil that it took them three days to gather it.

L.25: And Jehoshaphat and his people came to plunder their spoil, and they found among them in abundance goods and corpses and precious articles, and they stripped [them] for themselves until [there was] no carrying [more]; and they were three days plundering the spoil, for it [was] so much.

R.25: Jehoshaphat and his soldiers went to take what the enemy had left behind. Among the dead bodies they found a great deal of equipment and valuable things, more than they could carry. There was so much that it took them three days to collect it all.

decisions.choice: corpses: the Hebrew text
alternatives: goods and garments and precious things
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text lists "corpses" among the things found, which is odd in a list of spoil; the goods were found on and among the bodies. Some Hebrew manuscripts and the ancient Latin translation read "garments" instead, a word that differs from "corpses" by one letter in Hebrew. This translation keeps the Hebrew text and reads the list as goods found with the dead.

decisions.choice: his people: his army
decisions.reason: "People" here are the soldiers who marched out with the king, as often in these books.

decisions.choice: until there was no carrying: more than they could carry
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says they took spoil "until there was no carrying": they could not carry any more.

decisions.choice: three days plundering: the size of the spoil
decisions.reason: The spoil was so great that it took three days to gather. The army that came to drive Judah out (verse 11) left Judah rich.

decisions.choice: with the dead (Balanced); among the dead bodies (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable place the corpses where the goods were found, which is how this translation reads the Hebrew list (m1). Balanced says "troops" and Readable "soldiers" for "people" (m2).

records.source: וּבַיּ֣וֹם הָרְבִעִ֗י נִקְהֲלוּ֙ לְעֵ֣מֶק בְּרָכָ֔ה כִּי־שָׁ֖ם בֵּרֲכ֣וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה עַל־כֵּ֡ן קָֽרְא֞וּ אֶת־שֵׁ֨ם הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֛וּא עֵ֥מֶק בְּרָכָ֖ה עַד־הַיּֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And on the day the fourth they assembled in [the] Valley of Beracah, for there they blessed Yahweh; therefore they have called [the] name of the place the that [the] Valley of Beracah until the day the this.
pieces: On the fourth day they gathered in the Valley of Beracah, for there they blessed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. That is why that place has been called the Valley of Beracah to this day.

L.26: And on the fourth day they assembled in the Valley of Beracah, for there they blessed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; therefore they have called the name of that place the Valley of Beracah to this day.

R.26: On the fourth day they gathered in a valley and praised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} there. That is why the place has been called the Valley of Beracah, or Valley of Blessing, to this day.

decisions.choice: Beracah: "blessing"
decisions.reason: The name means "blessing". It is explained by what the people did there: they blessed Yahweh. The place name and the verb come from the same root.

decisions.choice: blessed Yahweh: praised and thanked him
decisions.reason: When people bless God, they praise him and give him thanks for what he has done (1 Chronicles 29:10, 20).

decisions.choice: to this day: the writer's own day
decisions.reason: As in 5:9, "to this day" refers to the time of the writer or of the source he used: the name was still known then.

decisions.choice: or Valley of Blessing
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the name (m1) so that the reader sees why it was given. Literal and Balanced keep the name and leave the meaning to the note.

records.source: וַ֠יָּשֻׁבוּ כָּל־אִ֨ישׁ יְהוּדָ֤ה וִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ וִֽיהוֹשָׁפָ֣ט בְּרֹאשָׁ֔ם לָשׁ֥וּב אֶל־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בְּשִׂמְחָ֑ה כִּֽי־שִׂמְּחָ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה מֵֽאוֹיְבֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And returned every man of Judah and Jerusalem, and Jehoshaphat at their head, to return to Jerusalem with joy, for had made them rejoice Yahweh over their enemies.
pieces: Then all the men of Judah and Jerusalem, with Jehoshaphat leading them, returned joyfully to Jerusalem, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had given them joy over their enemies.

L.27: And every man of Judah and Jerusalem returned, with Jehoshaphat at their head, to go back to Jerusalem with joy, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had made them rejoice over their enemies.

R.27: Then all the men of Judah and Jerusalem went back home to Jerusalem, with Jehoshaphat leading them. They were full of joy, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had made them glad by defeating their enemies.

decisions.choice: made them rejoice over their enemies: gave them joy at their enemies' defeat
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says Yahweh made them rejoice "from" their enemies: their joy came from what God had done to the invaders.

decisions.choice: Jehoshaphat at their head: the king led the march home
decisions.reason: The king who had led them out in faith (verse 20) now leads them back in triumph.

decisions.choice: by defeating their enemies
decisions.reason: Readable says how God gave them joy (m1).

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם בִּנְבָלִ֥ים וּבְכִנֹּר֖וֹת וּבַחֲצֹצְר֑וֹת אֶל־בֵּ֖ית יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And they came [to] Jerusalem with harps and with lyres and with trumpets, to [the] house of Yahweh.
pieces: They came into Jerusalem with harps, lyres and trumpets, and went to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.28: And they came to Jerusalem with harps and with lyres and with trumpets, to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.28: They entered Jerusalem playing harps, lyres and trumpets, and went to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: harps, lyres and trumpets: the instruments of temple music
decisions.reason: These are the instruments of the Levite singers and the priests (5:12; 1 Chronicles 15:16, 24). The march ends in worship.

decisions.choice: to the house of Yahweh: back where the prayer was made
decisions.reason: The story ends where it began, at the temple where Jehoshaphat prayed (verse 5) and where God had promised to hear (verse 9).

decisions.choice: went (Balanced, Readable); playing (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add a verb for the last phrase, and Readable says the instruments were played.

records.source: וַיְהִי֙ פַּ֣חַד אֱלֹהִ֔ים עַ֖ל כָּל־מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת בְּשָׁמְעָ֕ם כִּ֚י נִלְחַ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה עִ֖ם אוֹיְבֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And was [the] dread of God on all [the] kingdoms of the lands when they heard that had fought Yahweh with [the] enemies of Israel.
pieces: When all the kingdoms of the lands heard that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had fought against Israel's enemies, the fear of God fell on them.

L.29: And the dread of God was on all the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had fought against the enemies of Israel.

R.29: When the kingdoms of other lands heard how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had fought against Israel's enemies, they were all terrified of God.

decisions.choice: the dread of God: a terror that God sent on the nations
decisions.reason: The phrase means terror before God, which kept the nations from attacking his people (14:13; 17:10; Genesis 35:5).

decisions.choice: fought with: fought against
decisions.reason: "With" after the verb "fight" means "against", as in verse 6.

decisions.choice: Israel: God's people, here Judah
decisions.reason: Chronicles often calls Judah "Israel", as the people of God who kept the true worship (12:6; 21:2). The enemies attacked Judah.

decisions.choice: the hearing first; terrified
decisions.reason: Readable puts the news first and the result after, and says "terrified" for "dread".

records.source: וַתִּשְׁקֹ֖ט מַלְכ֣וּת יְהוֹשָׁפָ֑ט וַיָּ֧נַֽח ל֦וֹ אֱלֹהָ֖יו מִסָּבִֽיב׃פ
records.gloss: And was quiet [the] kingdom of Jehoshaphat, and gave rest to him his God from around.
pieces: So Jehoshaphat's kingdom had peace, for his God gave him rest on every side.

L.30: And the kingdom of Jehoshaphat was quiet, and his God gave him rest all around.

R.30: So Jehoshaphat's kingdom was at peace. His God gave him rest from enemies on every side.

decisions.choice: his God gave him rest all around: the blessing promised to the faithful
decisions.reason: Rest from enemies is God's gift to a king who seeks him, as for Solomon (1 Chronicles 22:9) and Asa (14:5-6; 15:15).

decisions.choice: was quiet: had peace
decisions.reason: The verb means to be undisturbed, free of war, as in Judges (3:11).

decisions.choice: had peace (Balanced); was at peace (Readable)
decisions.reason: "The land was quiet" is rendered "had peace" at Balanced, as in Judges. Readable adds "from enemies" to say what the rest was.

records.source: וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט עַל־יְהוּדָ֑ה בֶּן־שְׁלֹשִׁים֩ וְחָמֵ֨שׁ שָׁנָ֜ה בְּמָלְכ֗וֹ וְעֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ מָלַ֣ךְ בִּֽירוּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ עֲזוּבָ֖ה בַּת־שִׁלְחִֽי׃
records.gloss: And reigned Jehoshaphat over Judah, a son of thirty and five years when he became king, and twenty and five years he reigned in Jerusalem; and [the] name of his mother [was] Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
pieces: Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he became king. He reigned in Jerusalem twenty-five years, and his mother's name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.

L.31: And Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. [He was] thirty-five years old when he became king, and twenty-five years he reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother [was] Azubah daughter of Shilhi.

R.31: Jehoshaphat ruled over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for twenty-five years. His mother was Azubah, the daughter of Shilhi.

decisions.choice: Jehoshaphat's reign: told also in 1 Kings 22:41-42
decisions.reason: The summary of verses 31-34 follows 1 Kings 22:41-46, and the wording here follows it where the Hebrew is the same. Chronicles leaves out the date by the reign of Ahab king of Israel and the words "son of Asa", and joins the two verses of Kings into one.

decisions.choice: a son of thirty-five years: thirty-five years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being "a son of" so many years.

decisions.choice: the name of his mother: the queen mother
decisions.reason: For the kings of Judah, the account names each king's mother, who held an honored place at court (15:16).

decisions.choice: thirty-five years old
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 22:42, every level gives the age in the normal English way (m2).

records.heading: The end of Jehoshaphat's reign

records.source: וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ בְּדֶ֛רֶךְ אָבִ֥יו אָסָ֖א וְלֹא־סָ֣ר מִמֶּ֑נָּה לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he walked in [the] way of his father Asa and not he turned aside from it, doing the right in [the] eyes of Yahweh.
pieces: He followed the ways of his father Asa and did not turn aside from them, doing what was right in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.32: And he walked in the way of his father Asa, and he did not turn aside from it, doing the right in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.32: He lived the way his father Asa had lived and never turned away from it. He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was right.

decisions.choice: he walked in the way of his father Asa: as 1 Kings 22:43, without "all"
decisions.reason: Kings says Jehoshaphat walked "in all the way" of Asa. Chronicles leaves out "all". It has told of Asa's failures late in his reign (16:7-12), and it praises Jehoshaphat for seeking God as Asa had done in his early years (17:3-4).

decisions.choice: walked in the way of: lived as he had lived
decisions.reason: To walk in someone's way is to follow his example.

decisions.choice: doing the right in [the] eyes of / doing what was right in the sight of / did what the LORD said was right
decisions.reason: The verdict formula has one wording at each level throughout these books, as in 1 Kings 22:43.

records.source: אַ֥ךְ הַבָּמ֖וֹת לֹא־סָ֑רוּ וְע֤וֹד הָעָם֙ לֹא־הֵכִ֣ינוּ לְבָבָ֔ם לֵאלֹהֵ֖י אֲבֹתֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Only the high places not were removed, and still the people not had set their heart to [the] God of their fathers.
pieces: However, the high places were not removed, and the people had still not fixed their hearts on the God of their ancestors.

L.33: Only the high places were not removed, and the people had not yet set their heart on the God of their fathers.

R.33: But the hilltop shrines were not removed. The people still had not given their hearts fully to the God of their ancestors.

decisions.choice: the people had not yet set their heart: a difference from 1 Kings 22:44
decisions.reason: Kings says that the people still sacrificed and burned incense at the high places. Chronicles gives the reason behind it: the people's hearts were not yet fixed on God.

decisions.choice: the high places were not removed: set against 17:6
alternatives: the king removed the high places early in his reign, but the people kept them
decisions.reason: In 17:6 Chronicles says Jehoshaphat removed the high places and the Asherah poles from Judah. The two statements may be read together in more than one way: the king removed the shrines of other gods, but local shrines where Yahweh was worshiped remained; or he removed them, but the people, whose hearts were not fixed on God, kept or rebuilt them. Chronicles says the same two things of Asa (14:2; 15:17).

decisions.choice: the high places: local places of worship
decisions.reason: High places were local shrines, often on hills. Even when used to worship Yahweh, they went against the law's demand to worship at the one place he chose (Deuteronomy 12:13-14).

decisions.choice: set their heart on: firmly commit themselves to
decisions.reason: To set or fix the heart is to commit oneself to something with full purpose (12:14; 19:3).

decisions.choice: hilltop shrines; given their hearts fully
decisions.reason: Readable says "hilltop shrines" for high places, as these books do throughout, and explains "set their heart" (m4).

records.source: וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוֹשָׁפָ֔ט הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים וְהָאַחֲרֹנִ֑ים הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים בְּדִבְרֵי֙ יֵה֣וּא בֶן־חֲנָ֔נִי אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֹֽעֲלָ֔ה עַל־סֵ֖פֶר מַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Jehoshaphat, the first and the last, behold they [are] written in [the] words of Jehu son of Hanani, which was taken up into [the] book of the kings of Israel.
pieces: The rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, from first to last, are written in the records of Jehu son of Hanani, which are included in the Book of the Kings of Israel.

L.34: And the rest of the matters of Jehoshaphat, the first and the last, see, they [are] written in the words of Jehu son of Hanani, which were taken up into the book of the kings of Israel.

R.34: Everything else Jehoshaphat did, from beginning to end, is written in the records of Jehu son of Hanani. These records were included in the book of the kings of Israel.

decisions.choice: the words of Jehu ... the book of the kings of Israel: a difference from 1 Kings 22:46
decisions.reason: Kings sends the reader to "the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah" and mentions Jehoshaphat's might and wars. Chronicles names a prophet's account, as it often does (9:29; 12:15), and says that account was taken into a larger book of the kings.

decisions.choice: Jehu son of Hanani: the prophet who rebuked Jehoshaphat
decisions.reason: Jehu had spoken against Baasha king of Israel (1 Kings 16:1, 7) and against Jehoshaphat for helping Ahab (19:2). His father Hanani was also a seer (16:7).

decisions.choice: taken up into: recorded in, made part of
decisions.reason: The verb means "brought up" or "entered": Jehu's account was copied into the book of the kings.

decisions.choice: the kings of Israel: the kings of God's people, including Judah's
decisions.reason: Chronicles uses "Israel" for the whole people of God, so this book of "the kings of Israel" includes Judah's kings (verse 29; compare 16:11, "the kings of Judah and Israel").

decisions.choice: see, they are written: a statement, not a question
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew states that the records exist; it does not use the question form of Kings.

decisions.choice: the accounts (Balanced); the records (Readable); included
decisions.reason: As in 12:15, Balanced says "accounts" and Readable "records" for "words". The book's title is capitalized at Balanced, as source titles are.

records.source: וְאַחֲרֵי כֵ֗ןאֶתְחַבַּר֙ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֣ט מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֔ה עִ֖ם אֲחַזְיָ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ה֖וּא הִרְשִׁ֥יעַ לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃
records.gloss: And after so joined himself Jehoshaphat king of Judah with Ahaziah king of Israel; he acted wickedly to do.
pieces: Later on, Jehoshaphat king of Judah joined in an alliance with Ahaziah king of Israel, a man who acted wickedly.

L.35: And after this Jehoshaphat king of Judah joined himself with Ahaziah king of Israel, who acted wickedly in [his] doing.

R.35: Later, King Jehoshaphat of Judah made an agreement with King Ahaziah of Israel, who did what was evil.

decisions.choice: he acted wickedly: Ahaziah, who did evil
alternatives: he acted wickedly in doing so (Jehoshaphat)
decisions.reason: The short clause "he acted wickedly to do" most naturally describes Ahaziah, who did evil in Yahweh's sight (1 Kings 22:52-53). It can also be read of Jehoshaphat: "he acted wickedly in doing so", in making the alliance. Either way the alliance is condemned (verse 37).

decisions.choice: joined himself with: made an alliance with
decisions.reason: The verb means to join or bind oneself. It returns in verses 36 and 37, where the prophet names it as the reason for judgment.

decisions.choice: an alliance with Israel's king again: after the rebuke of 19:2
decisions.reason: Jehu had rebuked Jehoshaphat for helping Ahab, "one who hates Yahweh" (19:2). Now he joins Ahab's son Ahaziah.

decisions.choice: made an agreement
decisions.reason: Readable says "made an agreement" for the alliance and "did what was evil" for "acted wickedly".

records.source: וַיְחַבְּרֵ֣הוּ עִמּ֔וֹ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת אֳנִיּ֖וֹת לָלֶ֣כֶת תַּרְשִׁ֑ישׁ וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ אֳנִיּ֖וֹת בְּעֶצְי֥וֹן גָּֽבֶר׃
records.gloss: And he joined him with him to make ships to go [to] Tarshish, and they made ships in Ezion-geber.
pieces: He joined with him in building ships to go to Tarshish, and they built the ships at Ezion-geber.

L.36: And he joined him with himself to make ships to go [to] Tarshish, and they made ships in Ezion-geber.

R.36: The two kings agreed to build ships together to sail to Tarshish. They built the ships at Ezion-geber.

decisions.choice: ships to go to Tarshish: a difference from 1 Kings 22:49
decisions.reason: Kings says Jehoshaphat made "ships of Tarshish", large seagoing ships, "to go to Ophir" for gold. Chronicles says the ships were "to go to Tarshish", as it does of Solomon's ships (9:21). It may take Tarshish as the goal, or use the phrase for the long voyages such ships made. Ezion-geber lay on the Red Sea, far from the Mediterranean, which suggests the second.

decisions.choice: he joined him with him: Jehoshaphat made Ahaziah his partner
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in verse 35. The two kings built the fleet together; Kings tells only of Jehoshaphat's ships.

decisions.choice: Ezion-geber: a port on the Red Sea
decisions.reason: Ezion-geber lay at the northern tip of the Gulf of Aqaba, in Edom's territory, where Solomon had built his fleet (8:17).

decisions.choice: the two kings agreed to build ships together
decisions.reason: Readable says who joined with whom.

records.source: וַיִּתְנַבֵּ֞א אֱלִיעֶ֤זֶר בֶּן־דֹּדָוָ֨הוּ֙ מִמָּ֣רֵשָׁ֔ה עַל־יְהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט לֵאמֹ֑ר כְּהִֽתְחַבֶּרְךָ֣ עִם־אֲחַזְיָ֗הוּ פָּרַ֤ץ יְהוָה֙ אֶֽת־מַעֲשֶׂ֔יךָ וַיִּשָּׁבְר֣וּ אֳנִיּ֔וֹת וְלֹ֥א עָצְר֖וּ לָלֶ֥כֶת אֶל־תַּרְשִֽׁישׁ׃
records.gloss: And prophesied Eliezer son of Dodavahu of Mareshah against Jehoshaphat, saying, Because you joined yourself with Ahaziah, has broken Yahweh your works. And were wrecked [the] ships and not they were able to go to Tarshish.
pieces: Then Eliezer son of Dodavahu from Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat: "Because you have allied yourself with Ahaziah, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will break down what you have made." And the ships were wrecked and could not sail to Tarshish.

L.37: And Eliezer son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, "Because you have joined yourself with Ahaziah, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has broken down your works." And the ships were broken, and they were not able to go to Tarshish.

R.37: Then a man named Eliezer son of Dodavahu, from the town of Mareshah, gave a message from God against Jehoshaphat. He said, "You have joined with Ahaziah, so {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will destroy what you have built." The ships were wrecked and never sailed to Tarshish.

decisions.choice: has broken down: a judgment as sure as if already done
decisions.reason: The verb is in the past tense, but it announces what Yahweh is about to do: the prophet speaks of the coming wreck as already settled.

decisions.choice: the ships were wrecked: told also in 1 Kings 22:49-50
decisions.reason: Kings says the ships were wrecked at Ezion-geber but gives no reason, and says that Jehoshaphat then refused Ahaziah's offer to send his men with Jehoshaphat's on the ships. Chronicles names the alliance as the reason and gives the prophet's word. The two accounts may tell different stages: after the wreck and the warning, Jehoshaphat would not join Ahaziah again.

decisions.choice: Mareshah: a town in the lowland of Judah
decisions.reason: Mareshah lay in the foothills west of Hebron; Rehoboam fortified it (11:8), and Asa fought the Cushites near it (14:8-9).

decisions.choice: because you joined with Ahaziah: God judges the alliance with a wicked king
decisions.reason: As Jehu warned (19:2), joining with a king who rejected Yahweh brought God's judgment, here the loss of the fleet.

decisions.choice: your works: what you have made, the ships
decisions.reason: "Works" are the things a person makes or does; here, the fleet built at Ezion-geber.

decisions.choice: will break down (Balanced); will destroy (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the future tense for the prophet's announcement (m1). Readable says "gave a message from God" for "prophesied".
